question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{"><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfenced></math> be a relation on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> be the equivalence relation on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>S</mi></math> and the number of elements in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>. Then, the minimum value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> is _______

solution.text:
Given,

A=1, 2, 3, 4 and R=(1, 2), (2, 3), (1, 4) be a relation on A.

Now, given S be the equivalence relation on A and R⊂S

So, for S to be equivalence it should be Reflexive, Symmetric and Transitive on given relation,

Now, for reflexive Relation we need, 1,1, 2,2, 3,3, 4,4→4 elements,

For Symmetric relation we need, 2,1, 3,2, 4,1→3 elements,

And for Transitive relation we need, 1,3, 3,1, 3,4, 4,2, 2,4, 4,3→6 elements

So, minimum 13 elements should be added in R

Hence , nS=16 elements.
